classification: post-development single-topic transport repair verification, not independent held-out acceptance
boundaries: The earlier 10-second failure had no header/body telemetry; its failed transport stage remains unknown. This run tests a bounded phase-budget hypothesis, not a proven root cause.
Use production JobService, OfficialSitemapProvider and phased PinnedHTTPClient. No saved report XML, seeded loc/course URL, altered ranking, Range request, replacement IP or retry.
Only MIT same-origin HTTPS, robots actually declared index and actual child loc URLs. One original probability point and at most one matching child sitemap.
All target HTTP including robots/index/child/page/redirect/catalog share six requests. Actual A/AAAA DoH HTTP share twelve requests and are separately traced.

First response remains bounded by 10 seconds; body idle is bounded by 5 seconds, fixed body total by min(byte-cap/32768,10) seconds; no chunk resets total deadline. Each target is bounded by 20 seconds, whole run by 120 seconds.
XML paths have a 500000-byte cap, including root sitemap; every target remains below the existing 2000000-byte cap. No compressed bodies, unsafe redirect or implicit proxy.
Stop all subsequent network on access restriction, network/DNS/size error, deadline or total budget. Preserve first failure/partial results without replacement or rerun.
A complete index-to-course/page evidence chain is the target; catalogue, video structure and playback are separate outcomes. Never count partial body/hash as successful source evidence.
Isolated fresh SQLite only. Preserve original probe, failed repair and held-out reports by hash; root separately authorizes the single external execution.
